page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24 is a compute-focused server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing two threads per core. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and is equipped with 90.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The processor architecture is x86_64, featuring a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

This server configuration does not include local NVMe SSD storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring external networking configurations for public internet access.

In benchmark testing, the c4-standard-24 demonstrates solid performance across various workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1912.0 and a multi-core score of 13690.0. Image processing and text processing benchmarks show strong performance, placing in the top 25% with scores of 13744.0 and 2618.0 respectively. For machine learning workloads, the instance achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small 135M LLM models at 396.71 tokens per second, though performance scales down to 17.23 tokens per second for medium 7B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-24 offers a balanced resource density for compute-heavy tasks that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving with up to 41.15 GB/sec throughput, database operations, and lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference.
